14 Two forces, each of magnitude F, act in opposite directions on a rod.

Each force acts on the rod at a distance d from the pivot P.
What is the torque of this couple about P?
A
0
B
F  d
C
2F  d
D
2F  2d

hints: Notice the diagram shows one $F$ upward at distance $d$ left of P and one $F$ downward at distance $d$ right of P.
Check the rotational sense of each $F$ about P using moment $=$ force $\times$ perpendicular distance.
Add the two moments about P rather than subtracting them, since a couple has two turning effects in the same direction.
walkthrough: Identify the given data from the diagram: left force $F$ upward with perpendicular distance $d$ from P, and right force $F$ downward with perpendicular distance $d$ from P.
Recall that moment about a point is $\text{moment} = F \times d$ with perpendicular distance, and clockwise and anticlockwise senses must be compared.
Left force: $r = d$ to the left with upward $F$ gives moment $F \times d$ tending to rotate the rod clockwise about P.
Right force: $r = d$ to the right with downward $F$ gives moment $F \times d$ also tending to rotate the rod clockwise about P.
Add the like-sense moments for total torque about P: $F \times d + F \times d = 2F \times d$.

A.explanation: The resultant force is zero but the turning effects do not cancel because both $F$ forces tend to turn the rod the same way about P.

B.explanation: This is the moment of only one force about P, $F \times d$, and misses the second equal turning effect on the other side.

C.explanation: Both moments about P are $F \times d$ in the same rotational sense, so total torque is $F \times d + F \times d = 2F \times d$.

D.explanation: This multiplies by the separation $2d$ twice; the couple torque is one force times separation, $F \times 2d$, not $2F \times 2d$.
